transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what finally pushed me to make an appointment is that my eating has just been all over the place lately. Um, some weeks I barely even touch dinner. And then... other nights, I find myself just standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone else has gone to bed. It's just been really inconsistent.
During those nighttime eating episodes, do you feel like you can't control how much you're eating or stop yourself once you start?

No, I wouldn't say I feel out of control. Um... it's not like I can't stop myself. I just sort of grab a few things because I'm awake and feel like having a snack, but I can stop whenever I want to. It's just odd for me to be eating at that hour.
On the nights you eat crackers and sweets, do you actually wake up from sleep and then feel you need to eat before you can fall back asleep, or are you just still awake and haven't gone to bed yet?

No, I'm just still awake. Um... I haven't gone to bed yet when it happens. It's not like I'm waking up from sleep and feeling like I have to eat to get back to bed. I'm just up late, usually long after everyone else is asleep, and I end up grabbing something from the kitchen before I finally try to go to sleep.
On the nights when you're up late eating, is it because you're having trouble falling asleep once you do try, or do you just naturally stay up later and haven't attempted to sleep yet?

Well, it's not that I'm trying to sleep and can't. It's more that... I just don't feel tired. Lately, I can sleep maybe three or four hours, and when I wake up, I feel completely charged. I'm ready to write blog posts or start planning out new projects before the sun is even up. So, I just stay up because I have all this energy.
How long has this period of needing only three to four hours of sleep and feeling full of energy and ideas been going on?

Well, these stretches where I'm just so energized and taking on all these new projects... they've been happening for a while now. I'd say it's been about a year and eight months since I first started noticing it.

Over this past year and eight months, have there also been stretches where your mood or energy dropped much lower than usual—feeling down, low energy, or less interested in things—in between these energized periods?

Yeah, there have been. Um... I do go through these stretches where the whole house just feels really gray and heavy. I'll just sit there at the kitchen table feeling empty, even though nothing terrible has actually happened that day. So, yes, I definitely get those low periods in between the energized ones.
When you're in one of these energized, high-productivity phases, about how many days in a row does it usually last before your mood or energy shifts again?
Um, I'm not really sure exactly how many days it lasts. I haven't really kept track of it like that. It just kind of goes on for a bit, and then eventually it stops and things shift again.
When you're in one of those low, 'gray and heavy' periods, about how many days in a row does that usually last before it lifts?

I'm not exactly sure how many days in a row each one lasts, either. But... if I look at the whole timeframe, those gray, guilty periods where I just lose interest in things have added up to about seven months altogether.

Over this past year and eight months, have there been any stretches of two months or longer where your mood and energy felt basically normal, without either the energized highs or the gray, low periods?

Well, I haven't had a full two months where everything felt completely normal. I mean, I've had stretches of several weeks at a time where my mood wasn't really high or really low. But even during those weeks, I... I still felt certain that people online were tracking the photos I post of my garden. And I'd still hear those brief remarks or voices when I was alone in the house. So, no, not a full two months of everything being completely normal.

Thinking about those weeks when your mood felt neither high nor low, did the feeling that people were tracking your garden photos and hearing those voices continue every day throughout that whole stretch, or did those experiences only pop up occasionally?

Well, like I was just saying, I've had several weeks at a time when my mood wasn't especially high or low, but I still felt sure people online were tracking my garden photos. And I still heard those brief remarks when I was alone. It didn't just go away... it was happening pretty much every day throughout that whole stretch, not just occasionally.
